text:
Miro Heiskanen came back on Nov. 17 after missing two weeks and scored the overtime winner against Vegas in his first game, then opened the scoring against the same team two nights later. Dallas hasn't lost with him back. He's playing more than 25 minutes a night, and the Stars have taken 54% of the expected goals, the share of quality chances, with him on at five on five, 5.5 points better than without him.

The goals are the part that won't last. He has five on 2.1 expected, shooting 17% after 6% last season. Our range for a defenseman's finishing puts his true rate between 5.5% and 9%, so the goal column should slow while the minutes and the play driving stay.

Evolving-Hockey had him 12th among defensemen last season, though it flagged that his results ran ahead of his chances then too. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds a habit to watch: he shoots a lot, 89th percentile in attempts, but fewer from the slot than the volume suggests. If he gets inside more, the scoring can hold up. If not, expect assists to carry the line.
